10.1 Notch sensitivity and fatigue stress-concentration factor

  • Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1), or Kfs = 1 + q_shear(Kts − 1) [MD-F p.3].
  • Notch-sensitivity chart for steels and UNS A92024-T wrought aluminum alloys in reversed bending or reversed axial load. The curves are Sut = 200 kpsi (1.4 GPa), 150 (1.0), 100 (0.7) and 60 (0.4) for steels, dashed for the aluminum alloy; notch radius r = 0–0.16 in (0–4 mm) [MD-F p.3].
  • For larger notch radii, use the q value at r = 0.16 in (4 mm) [MD-F p.3].
  • The second chart gives q_shear for reversed torsion, with the same curve set; for larger radii use the value at r = 0.16 in (4 mm) [MD-F p.3].
  • No Neuber-constant formula for q is given; q is read from the charts [MD-F p.3].

10.2 Fluctuating stresses and failure criteria

  • Fm = (Fmax + Fmin)/2; Fa = |(Fmax − Fmin)/2| [MD-F p.4].
  • σm = (σmax + σmin)/2; σa = |(σmax − σmin)/2| [MD-F p.4].
  • Stress ratio R = σmin/σmax; amplitude ratio A = σa/σm [MD-F p.4].
  • Stress-time patterns shown: general fluctuating, repeated, completely reversed [MD-F p.5].
  • Failure lines [MD-F p.6]:
    • Soderberg: Sa/Se + Sm/Sy = 1
    • modified Goodman: Sa/Se + Sm/Sut = 1
    • Gerber: Sa/Se + (Sm/Sut)² = 1
    • ASME-elliptic: (Sa/Se)² + (Sm/Sy)² = 1
  • Design forms with factor of safety n [MD-F p.6]:
    • Soderberg: σa/Se + σm/Sy = 1/n
    • mod-Goodman: σa/Se + σm/Sut = 1/n
    • Gerber: nσa/Se + (nσm/Sut)² = 1
    • ASME-elliptic: (nσa/Se)² + (nσm/Sy)² = 1

Stress-concentration charts

[MD-K]

  • The file reproduces Shigley Table A-15, "Charts of Theoretical Stress-Concentration Factors Kt*" (book pp. 1026–1032), and Table A-16 (book pp. 1033–1034) [MD-K p.1–9].
  • Most factors are from R. E. Peterson, "Design Factors for Stress Concentration," Machine Design, vol. 23, 1951 [MD-K p.2, p.4, p.5].
  • How to read a chart: compute the geometry ratios (d/w, r/d, D/d, a/t and so on). Enter the abscissa, move up to the curve for the second ratio (interpolating between curves), and read Kt (or Kts) on the ordinate. The peak stress is Kt σ0, where σ0 is the nominal stress defined in each chart's caption [MD-K p.1–7].
  • To get the fatigue factor, combine Kt with q from [MD-F] via Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1) [MD-F p.3].

12.2 PQ1: Final 2023, Problem 3 (55 marks) [MD-IP]

Statement [MD-IP p.1–2]

  • A torque T = 100 N·m is applied to shaft EFG, which runs at constant speed and carries spur gear F. Gear F transmits torque through gear C to shaft ABCD, which drives the chain sprocket B, transmitting a force P (Figure 3). Sprocket B, gear C and gear F have pitch diameters a = 150, b = 250 and c = 125 mm; pressure angle φ = 20°; no frictional losses; bearings at A, D, E, G are simple supports [MD-IP p.1].
  • Figure (3), gear and sprocket assembly: shaft ABCD of diameter d = 30 mm with x along the shaft; A at x = 0, sprocket B at e = 75 mm from A, gear C at f = 250 mm from B, bearing D at g = 125 mm from C (so B at 75, C at 325, D at 450 mm); the end view shows c = 125 mm (gear F), b = 250 mm (gear C) and a = 150 mm (sprocket) with the chain load P pointing down [MD-IP p.2]. See md2-2023-gear-sprocket-assembly.jpg.
  • Questions [MD-IP p.1]: (a) force P, 3 marks; (b) bearing reactions at A and D, 10 marks; (c) basic load rating C10 at A (ball bearing), 10 marks, for input shaft EG at 191 rev/min, life 12 kh, reliability for the ensemble of all four bearings (both shafts) ≥ 0.8145, manufacturer 2, application factor 1; (d) numbers of full-depth teeth on gears F and C to minimise size and avoid interference, 5 marks (motor 2 kW at 191 rev/min, a gear unit halves the motor speed); (e) module for gear F if its initial pitch diameter is 125 mm, 2 marks; (f) radial, tangential and total forces between F and C, 5 marks; (g) bending factor of safety of spur gear F, 10 marks; (h) surface-wear factor of safety of gear F, 10 marks.
  • Data for (g), (h) [MD-IP p.1]: both gears Grade 2 carburized and hardened steel; face width 4 times the circular pitch; life 12 kh, reliability 95 %; quality standard No. 6, uncrowned teeth, open gearing; Ko = KB = KT = ZR = Cpm = Ce = 1; size factor Ks = 1/kb = 0.8433(mF√Y)^0.0535 (SI).

Solution (as written)

  • Tangential force on gear F: Wt·Dc/2 = T gives 100 = Wt(0.125/2), Wt = 1600 N [MD-IP p.3]. Total force F = Wt/cos 20° = 1702.68 N [MD-IP p.3]. The radial component is 1702.68 sin 20° = 582.4 N [MD-IP p.4].
  • Torque on shaft ABCD: T = Wt·Db/2 = 1600(0.250/2) = 200 N·m [MD-IP p.3].
  • (a) TB = TC = 200 N·m = P(0.150/2), so P = 2666.666 N = 2667 N [MD-IP p.4].
  • (b) Equilibrium of shaft ABCD, y up, forces (y): −P at B, −582.4 at C, reactions Ay, Dy; forces (z): +1600 at C, reactions Az, Dz [MD-IP p.4–5]:
    • ΣFy: Ay − 2667 − 582.4 + Dy = 0 (1); ΣFz: Az + Dz − 1600 = 0 (2) [MD-IP p.4].
    • ΣMy = 0: −0.45 Dz + 0.325(1600) = 0, so Dz = 1155.55 ≈ 1156 N [MD-IP p.5].
    • ΣMz = 0: −P(0.075) − 582.4(0.325) + 0.45 Dy = 0, so Dy = 865.12 N [MD-IP p.5].
    • From (1): Ay = 2384.28 N; from (2): Az = 444 N [MD-IP p.6].
    • Radial loads: RA = √(2384.28² + 444²) = 2425.268 N; RD = √(865.12² + 1156²) = 1443.87 N [MD-IP p.6].
  • (c) Data: nd = 191 rev/min for gear F, ld = 12 × 10³ h, four bearings so R·R·R·R = 0.8145, written R = (0.8145)^(1/4) = 0.90249 ≈ 0.9025 (⚠ F22), af = 1, manufacturer 2 [MD-IP p.6]. Ball bearing at A: a = 3, LR = 1 × 10⁶, x0 = 0.02, θ = 4.459, b = 1.483 [MD-IP p.7].
    • Speed of the countershaft: df/dc = nc/nf gives 0.125/0.250 = nc/191, nc = 95 rev/min (written 95; 191/2 = 95.5) [MD-IP p.7].
    • xD = LD/LR = 60 nD ℓD/LR = 60(95)(12 × 10³)/(1 × 10⁶) = 68.4; FD = RA = 2425.268 N [MD-IP p.7].
    • C10 = af FD [xD/(x0 + (θ − x0)(1 − RD)^(1/b))]^(1/a) = 1(2425.268)[68.4/(0.02 + (4.459 − 0.02)(1 − 0.9025)^(1/1.483))]^(1/3) = 10 111.68 N ≈ 10.111 ≈ 10 kN [MD-IP p.7].
  • (d) K = 1 for full depth; mG = NG/NP = dG/dP = 250/125 = 2 [MD-IP p.8]. NP = [2K/((1 + 2m) sin²φ)][m + √(m² + (1 + 2m) sin²φ)] = [2(1)/((1 + 4) sin²20°)][2 + √(4 + 5 sin²20°)] = 14.16 ≈ 15 teeth (gear F); NF/NC = dF/dC gives 15/NC = 125/250, so NC = 30 teeth [MD-IP p.8].
  • (e) dF = 125 mm, m = d/N = 125/15 = 8.333 mm [MD-IP p.9].
  • (f) Arabic remark (partly legible): Wt is the one found before, only Wr is new; the power form gives almost the same number, which is a check. H = 2 kW, n = 191 rev/min, Wt = 60 000 H/(π d n) = 60 000(2)/(π(125)(191)) = 1.59988 kN ≈ 1600 N (kW, mm and kN; the π in the denominator is written like a "2" in the scan); F cos 20° = Wt gives F = 1.70256 kN = 1702.56 N; Wr = F sin 20° = 0.5823 kN ≈ 582.3 N [MD-IP p.9].
  • (g), (h) spur gear F, data: both gears Grade 2 carburized and hardened steel; F = b = 4p, p = πm = π(8.333) = 26.1789 mm, so F = b = 4(26.1789) = 104.7156 mm; ℓd = 12 × 10³ h, R = 95 %, Qv = 6, uncrowned, open gearing, Ko = KB = KT = ZR = Cpm = Ce = 1 [MD-IP p.10]. Equations used: σ = Wt Ko Kv Ks (1/(b mt))(KH KB/J); σc = ZE √(Wt Ko Kv Ks (KH/(dw b))(ZR/ZI)); SF = (St YN/(KT KR))/σ; SH = (Sc ZN CH/(KT KR))/σc [MD-IP p.11]. Wt = 1600 N [MD-IP p.11].
    • Kv = [(A + √(200V))/A]^B with B = 0.25(12 − Qv)^(2/3) = 0.25(12 − 6)^(2/3) = 0.825, A = 50 + 56(1 − B) = 50 + 56(1 − 0.825) = 59.8, V = πdn/60 = π(125/1000)(191/60) = 1.25 m/s; the printed result is Kv = 1.26 (⚠ F23) [MD-IP p.11].
    • Ks = 0.8433(mF√Y)^0.0535 with m = 8.333, F = 104.7156 mm, Y = 0.290 gives Ks = 1.172 [MD-IP p.11].
    • KH = 1 + Cmc(Cpf Cpm + Cma Ce) with Cpm = 1, Ce = 1, Cmc = 1; Cpf = b/(10d) − 0.0375 + 4.92 × 10⁻⁴ b = 104.7156/(10 × 125) − 0.0375 + 4.92 × 10⁻⁴(104.7156) = 0.097; Cma = A + BF + CF² with F = 104.7156 mm = 4.1226 in, A = 0.247, B = 0.0167, C = −0.765 × 10⁻⁴, giving Cma = 0.3145; KH = 1 + 1(0.097 × 1 + 0.3145 × 1) = 1.4115 [MD-IP p.12]. KB = 1; J = YJ = 0.25; mt = m = 8.333 mm [MD-IP p.12].
    • Bending stress: σ = 1600(1)(1.26)(1.172)[1/(104.7156 × 8.333/1000)][(1 × 1.4115)/0.25] = 15 287.844 N/m² written as σ = 15.287 MPa (the working prints the unit N/m² and converts to MPa) [MD-IP p.13].
    • Bending strength: KT = 1, St = 448 MPa; N = 60 nd ℓD = 60 × 191 × 12 × 10³ = 13 752 × 10⁴ rev (1.3752 × 10⁸); YN = 1.3558 N^−0.0178 = 0.9712; KR = 0.658 − 0.0759 ln(1 − R) = 0.658 − 0.0759 ln(1 − 0.95) = 0.8854 [MD-IP p.13].
    • SF = 448(0.9712)/0.8854/15.287 = 32.14 (bending, gear F) [MD-IP p.13].
    • Contact stress: ZI = [cos φt sin φt/(2 mN)][mG/(mG + 1)] = [cos 20° sin 20°/(2 × 1)][2/(2 + 1)] = 0.107; ZE = 191 √MPa; ZR = 1; KH = 1.4115; dw1 = 125 mm; b = 104.7156 mm [MD-IP p.13–14].
    • σc = 191 √(1600(1)(1.26)(1.172)(1.4115/(125 × 104.7156 × 10⁻⁶))(1/0.107)) = 191 × 1869.378917 (units √MPa·√(N/m²)) = 191 × 1.8693 × 10⁻³ … = 357.05 MPa (an earlier 0.357 GPa is struck out) (⚠ F24) [MD-IP p.14].
    • Wear strength: KT = 1, KR = 0.8854, Sc = 1551 MPa, ZN = 1.4488 N^−0.023 = 1.4488(13 752 × 10⁴)^−0.023 = 0.9415, CH = 1 [MD-IP p.14].
    • SH = 1551(0.9415)/(1 × 0.8854)/357.05 = 4.619 (wear, gear F); the result is boxed and struck with a large X; the same X (※) is drawn beside the final answer of most parts in these scans and appears to mark the end of a part, but the source does not explain it [MD-IP p.14].
  • Unreadable or unclear: the pages carry a CamScanner watermark; the small Arabic remark on p.9 is only partly legible [MD-IP p.9]. Cross-outs on p.5 cover earlier values of Dy (one reads 123.87) [MD-IP p.5].

12.3 PQ2: Final 2022–2023, Problem 2 (20 marks): cone clutch [MD-R1 p.1–3]

Statement [MD-R1 p.1]: a cone clutch has D = 12 in, d = 11 in, w = 2.305 in and a coefficient of friction 0.281. A torque of 1.8 kip·in is to be transmitted. Estimate the actuating force and the maximum pressure by both models (uniform wear and uniform pressure). The page also carries Figure (1), an internal rim-type brake (dimensions in millimetres, with a handwritten "24°"), and Figure (2), the cone clutch with cup, cone, spring, splined output shaft, shifting groove, half-angle α, pressure p, dFn and dr/sin α; a handwritten "b = ??" is beside the statement (the source does not say what it refers to). Figure (1) is cut off and its dimensions are unreadable [MD-R1 p.1].

Solution (as written) [MD-R1 p.2–3]

  • Data: D = d0 = 12 in, d = di = 11 in, f = 0.281, T = 1.8 kip·in, unknowns F and pa. sin α = ((D − d)/2)/w = 0.5/2.305, so α = 12.53° [MD-R1 p.2].
    1. Uniform wear: T = π f pa d (D² − d²)/(8 sin α); 1.8 × 10³ = π(0.281)(11) pa (12² − 1²)/(8 sin 12.53°) is written (the last term reads 1², not 11²), giving pa = 2.25 lbf/in² (⚠ F25). F = (π pa d/2)(D − d) = π(2.25)(11)/2 × (12 − 11) = 38.87 lbf (a second written value, 39, is struck out) [MD-R1 p.2].
    1. Uniform pressure: T = π f pa (D³ − d³)/(12 sin α); 1.8 × 10³ = π(0.281) pa (12³ − 11³)/(12 sin 12.58°) gives pa = 13.4 lbf/in² (α is written 12.58 here and 12.53 above) [MD-R1 p.2].
  • F = (π pa/4)(D² − d²) = π(13.4)/4 × (12² − 11²) = 242 lbf [MD-R1 p.3].
  • The foot of p.3 carries a handwritten Arabic note headed "Final 2022" that mentions Fo,tot, Fc,tot, C10 for bearing C, C10 for bearing D and "reaction" (it apparently says that the total bearing reactions are used for C10); it is only partly legible and is unrelated to the clutch [MD-R1 p.3].

12.4 PQ3: Final term exam 2023–2024, Problem 1 (60 marks): countershaft [MD-R1 p.4–11]

Statement [MD-R1 p.4–5]

  • Header (faint scan): Faculty of Engineering, 3rd year, Mechanical Design and Production Engineering, Machine Design, final term exam 2023–2024 (1st term), open-book exam, "Solve all questions", page 1 of 2, full marks 100; the date, the time, the course code and the examiner line are too faint to read reliably [MD-R1 p.5].
  • Figure Problem 3-83: shaft with bearings O and C, gear A (20 in dia) at 16 in from O, C at 14 in further, gear B (8 in dia) 9 in beyond C; FA = 300 lbf at 20° at gear A, FB at 20° at gear B; shaft diameter 1.25 in [MD-R1 p.4]. The slide heading reads "Determine factors of safety for bending and wear" (the textbook problem, solved in PQ4) [MD-R1 p.4].
  • A gear reduction unit uses this countershaft. Gear A receives power from another gear with force FA at the 20° pressure angle; the power leaves through gear B with force FB at the pressure angle shown [MD-R1 p.5].
  • (a) Determine FB at constant speed, 4 marks. (b) Find the bearing reaction forces (simple supports), 12 marks. The shaft rotates at 1200 rev/min, desired bearing life 10 kh with 95 % reliability in each bearing, manufacturer 2 in Table 11-6, application factor 1.3. (c) Ball bearings at O and C: obtain the basic load ratings C10, 12 marks. The gear ratio from gear B to its mating gear is 2 to 1. (d) Minimum number of teeth on gear B without interference, 5 marks. (e) Diametral pitch required to also achieve the 8-in pitch diameter, 3 marks [MD-R1 p.5].
  • Spur gear B drives a gear on the output shaft with a 2 to 1 speed reduction; all gears are of the same material; gear B is the smallest gear and transmits the largest load, so it is critical. Use a diametral pitch of 2 teeth/in, a face width of 4 times the circular pitch, a Grade 2 steel through-hardened to Brinell 300, life 15 kh with 95 % reliability, quality standard No. 6, uncrowned teeth, commercial enclosed gear unit, Ko = KB = KT = ZR = Ce = 1, size factor Ks = 1.192(F√Y/P)^0.0535 (the exponent is blurred in the scan). The statement continues on page 2 of the exam, which is not in the scan, so the questions (f) and (g) are not visible [MD-R1 p.5].

Solution (as written)

  • (a) TA = 300 cos 20°(20/2) = 2819 lbf·in ("N.lb.in" is written); TA = TB = FB cos 20°(8/2) gives FB = 749.97 ≈ 750 lbf. Arabic remark: the 750 is rounded to simplify the solution; in the exam, if the number comes out as an exact figure, write it as it comes [MD-R1 p.6].
  • (b) y–x plane: loads +300 cos 20° at A (x = 16), +Cy at C (x = 30), −750 sin 20° at B (x = 39), Oy at O; ΣMO: 300 cos 20°(16) + Cy(30) − 750 sin 20°(39) = 0 gives Cy = 183.1188 lbf; ΣFy: −Oy + 300 cos 20° + 183.1188 − 750 sin 20° = 0 gives Oy = 208.5114 lbf [MD-R1 p.7].
    • z–x plane: loads −300 sin 20° at A, −Cz at C, +750 cos 20° at B, +Oz at O; ΣMO: 300 sin 20°(16) + Cz(30) − 750 cos 20°(39) = 0 gives Cz = 861.477 lbf; Oz = 259.3135 lbf [MD-R1 p.8].
    • Totals: FO,tot = √(259.3135² + 208.5114²) = 332.746 lbf; FC,tot = √(183.1188² + 861.477²) = 880.724 lbf [MD-R1 p.8].
  • (c) n = 1200 rev/min, ℓD = 10 × 10³ h, R = 95 % for each bearing, manufacturer 2, af = 1.3, ball bearings at O and C; a = 3, LR = 1 × 10⁶, x0 = 0.02, θ = 4.459, b = 1.483; xD = LD/LR = 60(1200)(10 × 10³)/(1 × 10⁶) = 720 [MD-R1 p.9].
    • Bearing O: FD = 332.746 lbf; C10 = 1.3(332.746)[720/(0.02 + (4.459 − 0.02)(1 − 0.95)^(1/1.483))]^(1/3) = 4574.41 lbf [MD-R1 p.9–10].
    • Bearing C: FD = 880.724 lbf; C10 = 1.3(880.724)[…]^(1/3) = 12 107.717 lbf (written 12107.71695) [MD-R1 p.10]. The method uses (1 − R) rather than ln(1/R) (⚠ F26).
  • (d) mG = 2/1, K = 1 (full depth): NP = [2K/((1 + 2mG) sin²φ)][mG + √(mG² + (1 + 2mG) sin²φ)] = [2(1)/((1 + 2·2) sin²20°)][2 + √(2² + (1 + 2·2) sin²20°)] = 14.16 ≈ 15 teeth [MD-R1 p.10].
  • (e) NB = 15 teeth and d = 8 in: Pd = N/d = 15/8 = 1.875 teeth/in [MD-R1 p.11].
  • (f), (g): the note says these are solved as in the 2022 problem, "AGMA design" (PQ4) (Arabic remark) [MD-R1 p.11]. No separate numbers are given for the 2024 data (Pd = 2, life 15 kh, R = 95 %).
  • Unreadable or unclear: the exam header on p.5 is faint, and the ks exponent of the statement is blurred; the left margin of p.9 shows a cut-off Problem (1) about a brake mechanism ("… shoe … width of 40 … coefficient … pressure limit … estimate the … braking c…") and the start of the cone-clutch Problem (2), both unreadable beyond these fragments [MD-R1 p.9].

12.5 PQ4: Final 2022, Problem 3 (50 marks): countershaft in SI [MD-REV p.1–11; MD-R1 p.4; MD-R2 p.1–4]

Statement [MD-REV p.1–2]

  • A gear reduction unit (Figure 3: shaft 1 in, pinion C, gear A, pinion B, gear D, shaft 3 out, housing; bearings O and C on shaft 2) uses the countershaft (Shaft 2, Figure 4). Gear A receives power from pinion C with transmitted force FA at the 20° pressure angle; the power leaves through gear B with force FB at the pressure angle shown (25°) [MD-REV p.1–2].
  • Figure 4: FA = 11 kN at 20° on gear A (600 mm dia); distances 400 mm (O to A), 350 mm (A to B), 300 mm (B to C); gear B 300 mm dia; shaft diameter 50 mm; FB at 25° [MD-REV p.2]. See md2-2022-countershaft.jpg.
  • (a) FB at constant speed, 3 marks. (b) Bearing reactions (simple supports), 10 marks. Shaft 2 rotates at 900 rev/min, life 12 kh, reliability 98 % in each bearing, manufacturer 2 in Table 11-6, application factor 1.2. (c) Ball bearings at O and C: basic load ratings at O and C, 10 marks. Gear ratio from gear B to its mating gear is 5 to 1. (d) Minimum number of teeth on gear B without interference, 5 marks. (e) Using (d), the module required to also achieve the 300 mm pitch diameter, 2 marks [MD-REV p.1].
  • Spur gear B drives a gear on the output shaft with a 5 to 1 speed reduction; all gears are the same material; gear B is the smallest and most loaded, so it is critical. Module 18.75 mm/tooth, face width 4 times the circular pitch, Grade 2 steel through-hardened to 300 HB, life 12 kh, reliability 98 %, quality standard No. 6, uncrowned teeth, commercial enclosed gear unit, Ko = KB = KT = ZR = Ce = 1, Ks = 1/kb = 0.8433(mF√Y)^0.0535. St = 0.703 HB + 113 MPa (grade 2); Sc = 2.41 HB + 237 MPa (grade 2). (f) Factor of safety for bending, 10 marks; (g) for surface wear, 10 marks [MD-REV p.1].
  • The same problem is Shigley 14-38: "the countershaft in Problem 3-84 is part of a speed-reducing compound gear train using 20° spur gears. A gear on the input shaft drives gear A with a 2 to 1 speed reduction. Gear B drives a gear on the output shaft with a 5 to 1 speed reduction. The input shaft runs at 1800 rev/min. … module of 18.75 mm/tooth … 12 kh with a 98 percent reliability. Determine factors of safety for bending and wear" [MD-R2 p.1]. The US-unit figure on the same page (Problem 3-83, 300 lbf, 20-in and 8-in gears, 16/14/9 in) is the textbook figure [MD-R1 p.4; MD-R2 p.1] (⚠ F31).

Solution by the student (Final 2022, "Qu. No. 3") [MD-REV p.3–11]

  • Pressure angles: (φP)A = 20°, (φP)B = 25° [MD-REV p.3].
  • (a) TA = 11 cos 20°(600/2) = 3100.99 kN·mm; TA = TB = FB cos 25°(300/2) gives FB = 22.81 kN [MD-REV p.3].
  • (b) x–y plane: loads −11 sin 20° at A (x = 400), −22.81 sin 25° at B (x = 750), reactions Oy at O and Cy at C (x = 1050); ΣMO: 11 sin 20°(400) + 22.81 sin 25°(750) − Cy(1050) = 0 gives Cy = 8.3189 kN; ΣFy: Oy = 5.08 kN [MD-REV p.3–4].
    • x–z plane: −11 cos 20° at A, +22.81 cos 25° at B, +Oz at O, −Cz at C; ΣMO: 11 cos 20°(400) + Cz(1050) − 22.81 cos 25°(750) = 0 gives Cz = 10.83 kN; ΣFz gives Oz = 0.49 kN [MD-REV p.3–4].
    • Totals as written: FO,tot = √(5.08² + 8.3189²) = 9.747 kN; FC,tot = √(0.49² + 10.83²) = 10.8410 kN (the first term is handwritten so that it can be read as 6.49; only 0.49 gives 10.841) (⚠ F27) [MD-REV p.4].
  • (c) nd = 900 rev/min, ℓd = 12 kh, R = 98 % in each bearing, manufacturer 2, ball bearings at O and C, af = 1.2, LR = 1 × 10⁶ rev, x0 = 0.02, θ = 4.459, b = 1.483, a = 3; C10 = af FD [xD/(x0 + (θ − x0)(ln(1/RD))^(1/b))]^(1/a); xD = 60 nD ℓD/LR = 60(900)(12 × 10³)/(1 × 10⁶) = 648 [MD-REV p.4].
    • Bearing C: FD = 10.8410 kN; C10 = 1.2(10.8410 × 10³)[648/(0.02 + (4.459 − 0.02)(ln(1/0.98))^(1/1.483))]^(1/3) = 161 360.8 N = 161.36 kN [MD-REV p.4].
    • Bearing O: FD = 9.747 kN; C10 = 1.2(9.747 × 10³)[…]^(1/3) = 145.07 kN [MD-REV p.5].
  • (d) mG = 5/1, K = 1, φ = 25°: NB = [2(1)/((1 + 2·5) sin²25°)][5 + √(5² + (1 + 2·5) sin²25°)] = 10.376 ≈ 11 teeth [MD-REV p.5].
  • (e) dB = 300 mm: m = d/N = 300/11 = 27.27 mm [MD-REV p.5].
  • (f), (g) data restated: mG = 5; gear B is critical (Arabic remark: we saw from the shaft-design calculations that the critical section is at gear B); m = 18.75 mm/tooth; F = 4p = 4π/P = 4πm = 4π(18.75) = 235.62 mm (p = π/P, P = 1/m); Grade 2 steel through-hardened to 300 HB; ℓD = 12 kh; R = 98 %; Qv = 6; uncrowned; enclosed unit; Ko = KB = KT = ZR = Ce = 1 [MD-REV p.6].
    • Equations: SF = (St YN/(KT KR))/σ; SH = (Sc ZN CH/(KT KR))/σc; σ = Wt Ko Kv Ks (1/(b mt))(KH KB/J); σc = ZE √(Wt Ko Kv Ks (KH/(dw b))(ZR/ZI)) [MD-REV p.7].
    • Wt = FB cos 25° = 22.81 cos 25° = 20.672 kN. B = 0.25(12 − Qv)^(2/3) = 0.8254; A = 50 + 56(1 − B) = 59.7776; V = πdn = π(300/1000)(900/60) = 14.137 m/s; m = d/N gives 18.75 = 300/N, N = 16 teeth; written Kv = (59.7776 + √(200 × 14.137))/59.7776 = 1.89 (⚠ F28); Y = 0.296; Ks = 0.8433(18.75 × 235.62 × √0.296)^0.0535 = 1.28 [MD-REV p.7].
    • KH = Cmf = 1 + Cmc(Cpf Cpm + Cma Ce), Cmc = 1; Cpf = b/(10d) − 0.0375 + 4.92 × 10⁻⁴ b = 235.62/(10 × 300) − 0.0375 + 4.92 × 10⁻⁴(235.62) = 0.157; S1/S = 475/1050 = 0.45 and Cpm = 1.1; Cma = A + BF + CF² with F = 235.62 mm = 9.276 in, A = 0.127, B = 0.0158, C = −0.930 × 10⁻⁴, Cma = 0.2655; Ce = 1; KH = 1 + 1(0.157 × 1.1 + 0.265 × 1) = 1.4377 [MD-REV p.8].
    • KB = 1; J = (0.30 + 0.25)/2 = 0.275 [MD-REV p.9].
    • σ = 20.672 × 10³(1)(1.89)(1.28)[1/(235.62/1000 × 18.75)]·(1.4377 × 1/0.275) = 59 180.2 (units written N/m, meaning kPa) = 59.18 MPa [MD-REV p.9].
    • St = 0.703(300) + 113 = 323.9 MPa; KT = 1; N = 900(12 × 10³)(60) = 648 × 10⁶ rev; YN = 1.3558 N^−0.0178 written as 1.95 (⚠ F29); KR = 0.658 − 0.079 ln(1 − 0.98) = 0.967 [MD-REV p.9].
    • SF = 323.9(1.95)/(1 × 0.967)/59.18 = 5.65 (an earlier boxed value, apparently 11.03, is struck out and the final box carries a large X) [MD-REV p.9].
    • Contact: KH = 1.4377, Ko = 1, Kv = 1.89, Ks = 1.28, Wt = 20.672 × 10³ N, ZR = 1, b = 235.62 mm; I = [cos 25° sin 25°/(2 mN)][mG/(mG + 1)] = [cos 25° sin 25°/(2 × 1)][5/(5 + 1)] = 0.1595 (an earlier struck-out value is written first; the next line uses 0.1593) (⚠ F30) [MD-REV p.10].
    • ZE = 191 √MPa; dw = dp = mN = 16(18.75) = 300 mm (an Arabic note says the given 300 mm is confirmed); σc = 191 √(20.672 × 10³(1)(1.89)(1.28)(1.4377/(300 × 235.62/10³ × 10³))(1/0.1593)) = 191 × 2.5 √MPa = 482.636 MPa [MD-REV p.10].
    • Sc = 2.41(300) + 237 = 960 MPa; ZN = 1.4488 N^−0.023 = 1.4488(648 × 10⁶)^−0.023 = 0.908; CH = 1; KR = 0.967; KT = 1; SH = 960(0.908)/(1 × 0.967)/482.636 = 1.86 (boxed with a large X) [MD-REV p.10–11].

Textbook solution of the same problem (Shigley 14-38, SI) [MD-R2 p.1–4]

  • Data: m = 18.75 mm/tooth, d = 300 mm, N = d/m = 300/18.75 = 16 teeth, n = 1800/2 = 900 rev/min, F = b = 4p = 4π(18.75) = 236 mm [MD-R2 p.2].
  • ΣMx = 0: 300(11) cos 20° − 150 FB cos 25° gives FB = 22.81 kN; wt = FB cos 25° = 22.81 cos 25° = 20.67 kN; V = πdn/60 = π(0.3)(900)/60 = 14.14 m/s [MD-R2 p.2].
  • Strengths and factors [MD-R2 p.2–3]: Fig 14-2: St = 0.703(300) + 113 = 324 MPa; Fig 14-5: Sc = 2.41(300) + 237 = 960 MPa; Fig 14-6: J = Y_J = 0.27; Eq (14-23): I = ZI = [cos 20° sin 20°/(2(1))](5/(5 + 1)) = 0.134 (⚠ F30); Table 14-8: ZE = 191 MPa.
    • Qv = 6 assumed: B = 0.25(12 − Q)^(2/3) = (12 − 6)^(2/3) = 0.8255 (the printed line drops the factor 0.25); A = 50 + 56(1 − B) = 50 + (1 − 0.8255) = 59.77 (the printed line drops the 56); Eq (14-27): kv = [(59.77 + √(200 × 14.14))/59.77]^0.8255 = 1.69; Lewis form factor Y = 0.296 (Table 14-2) [MD-R2 p.2].
    • ks = 1/kb = 0.8433(mF√Y)^0.0535 = 0.8433(18.75 × 236 × √0.296)^0.0535 (result not printed; the later formulas use 1.28); d = 300/25.4 = 11.81 in, F = 236/25.4 = 9.29 in [MD-R2 p.3].
    • Cmc = 1 (uncrowned); Eq (14-32): Cpf = 9.29/(10 × 11.81) − 0.0375 + 0.0125(9.29) = 0.1573; Eq (14-33): Cpm = 1.1; Fig 14-11: Cma = 0.27 (commercial enclosed); Eq (14-35): Ce = 1; Eq (14-30): Km = KH = 1 + 1[0.1573(1.1) + 0.27(1)] = 1.44 [MD-R2 p.3].
    • N = 12 000 h (900 rev/min)(60 min/h) = 6.48(10⁸) rev; Fig 14-14: YN = 0.9; Fig 14-15: ZN = 0.85; Eq (14-38): KR = 0.658 − 0.0759 ln(1 − R) = 0.658 − 0.0759 ln(1 − 0.98) = 0.955; Ko = KB = KT = ZR = 1 [MD-R2 p.3].
    • Tooth bending, Eq (14-15): σ = Wt ko kv ks (1/(b mt))(KH kB/YJ) = 20 670(1)(1.69)(1.28)[1/(236(18.75))][(1.44)(1)/0.27] = 53.9 MPa [MD-R2 p.4].
    • Tooth wear, Eq (14-16): σc = ZE(Wt ko kv ks (kH/(dw b))(ZR/Z1))^(1/2) = 191[20 670(1)(1.69)(1.28)(1.44/(300 × 236))(1/0.134)]^(1/2) = 498 MPa [MD-R2 p.4].
    • Since gear B is a pinion, CH is not used in Eq (14-42): SH = Sc ZN/(KT KR)/σc = 960(0.85)/[(1)(0.955)]/498 = 1.72 [MD-R2 p.4]. The bending factor of safety is not printed on the captured pages (the page ends after SH).
  • Unreadable or unclear: MD-R2 pp.2–4 are phone screenshots with a phone status bar and page-boundary overlaps; MD-R2 p.3 repeats part of p.2. The unit line on MD-REV p.9 ("N/m") is a slip for kPa [MD-REV p.9].

12.6 PQ5: Problem 3 (25 marks), helical pinion, bearings and fatigue [MD-REV p.12–24]

Statement [MD-REV p.12]

  • In Figure 3 an electric motor transmits 1 hp at 1800 rev/min in the clockwise direction as viewed from the positive x axis. Keyed to the motor shaft is an 18-tooth helical pinion (18 T) with 1.4 in face width, normal pressure angle 20°, helix angle 30° and normal diametral pitch 12 teeth/in; the hand of the helix is shown in the figure (mating gear 36 T). Bearing A is 10 in from B, and the gear is 3 in beyond B along x [MD-REV p.12].
  • (a) Make a three-dimensional sketch of the motor shaft and gear shaft and show the forces acting at all bearings; for the motor shaft the thrust should be taken out at A. A ball bearing is to be selected at A to accept the thrust and a cylindrical roller bearing at B. The life goal of the speed reducer is 40 000 hours with a reliability factor for the ensemble of bearings of the motor shaft equal to 0.9604; application factor 1.5. (b) Select the roller bearing for location B. (c) Select the ball bearing (angular contact) for location A, assuming the inner ring rotates [MD-REV p.12].
  • (d) Assume the gear surface is machined and Sut = 55 kpsi, Sy = 30 kpsi, kd = ke = 1, kf = 1.66 (printed "1.6" with a blurred last digit): using the Soderberg equation, estimate the factor of safety of the gear based on an infinite life in bending [MD-REV p.12].
  • Handwritten margin formulas on p.12: Pn = Pt/cos ψ, Pn pn = π, Pn = Pt cos ψ, P = N/d (diametral pitch), m = d/N, and KF σall = S…/nd (the letter is unclear, probably Se) [MD-REV p.12].

Solution (as written)

  • Data: H = 1 hp, n = 1800 rev/min, NP = 18 T, F = 1.4 in, φn = 20°, ψ = 30°, Pn = 12 teeth/in [MD-REV p.13].
  • (a) Pn = Pt/cos ψ: 12 = Pt/cos 30°, Pt = 10.39 teeth/in. cos ψ = tan φn/tan φt gives φt = tan⁻¹(tan 20°/cos 30°) = 22.795° [MD-REV p.13].
    • dp = N/Pt = 18/10.39 = 1.73 in; V = πdn/12 = π(1.73)(1800)/12 = 815.24 ft/min (written 8015.24, a slip for 815.24); Wt = 33 000 H/V = 33 000(1)/815.1 = 40.493 lbf; Wr = Wt tan φt = 40.493 tan 22.795° = 17.31 lbf; Wa = Wt tan ψ = 40.493 tan 30° = 23.78 lbf (⚠ F32) [MD-REV p.13–14].
    • Free body of the motor shaft (x along the shaft, y up, z toward the viewer; A at x = 0, B at x = 10, load point at x = 13 with radius dp/2 = 1.73/2 = 0.865 in): Wr = 17.31 lbf, Wt = 41.193 lbf (written), Wa = 23.78 lbf [MD-REV p.14].
    • ΣFx: Ax = Wa = 23.78 lbf; ΣFy: Ay + By − 17.31 = 0 (1); ΣFz: Az + Bz + 41.193 = 0 (2); ΣMy = 0: −10 Bz − 13(41.193) = 0 gives Bz = −53.5509 lbf [MD-REV p.14].
    • ΣMz = 0: 10 By − 13 Wr + 0.865 Wa = 0, so 10 By − 13(17.31) + 0.865(23.78) = 0 gives By = 20.446 lbf; from (1) Ay = −3.136 lbf; from (2) Az = 12.3579 lbf [MD-REV p.14, p.16].
    • Summary sketch: Ax = 23.78 lbf, Ay = 3.136 (down), Az = 12.3579; By = 20.446 up, Bz = 53.5509 [MD-REV p.15].
  • Reliability and choices: ℓD = 40 000 h, R = 0.9604 for the ensemble (two bearings): R·R = 0.9604, R = √0.9604 = 0.98, af = 1.5; roller bearing at B, angular-contact ball bearing at A with the inner ring rotating [MD-REV p.15].
  • (b) Roller bearing B: FR = FD = √(53.5509² + 20.446²) = 57.32 lbf. Manufacturer 1 parameters (⚠ F35): LR = 90 × 10⁶, x0 = 0, θ = 4.48, b = 1.5; a = 10/3; T = 41.193(0.865) = 35.632 lbf·in, nD = 63 025 H/T = 63 025(1)/35.632 = 1768.77 (rev/min); xD = LD/LR = 60(1800)(40 000)/(90 × 10⁶) = 48 [MD-REV p.15, p.17].
    • C10 = af FD[xD/(x0 + (θ − x0)(ln(1/RD))^(1/b))]^(1/a) = 1.5(57.32)[48/((4.48)(ln(1/0.98))^(1/1.5))]^(3/10) = 382.21 lbf = 173.36 kg = 1700.73 N ≈ 1.7 kN (the exponent is written 3/10 for a = 10/3) [MD-REV p.17].
    • Arabic remark: the value must be converted to kN to enter the bearing table. Written: "Chose 02-25 mm, C10 = 16.8 kN" and, beside it, "03-25 mm, C10 = 28.6 kN", both circled, with a large X (b); which of the two is the final answer is not clear (⚠ F33) [MD-REV p.17]. The catalog table page is not among the pages of this file.
  • (c) Ball bearing A (angular contact): FR at A = √(3.136² + 12.3579²) = 12.75 lbf, Fa = 23.78 lbf; Fe = X V Fr + Y Fa with V = 1 (inner ring rotating); first assumption Y2 = 1.63, X2 = 0.56: Fe = 0.56(1)(12.75) + 1.63(23.78) = 45.9 ≈ 46 lbf [MD-REV p.18]. Ball bearing, a = 3; manufacturer 2: x0 = 0.02, θ = 4.459, b = 1.483, LR = 1 × 10⁶ [MD-REV p.18].
    • xD = 60 nD ℓD/LR = 60(1768.77)(40 000)/(1 × 10⁶) = 4245.6 (nD = 1768.77 from the torque check, not 1800) [MD-REV p.19].
    • First pass (Y2 assumed): C10 = 1.5(46)[4245.6/(0.02 + (4.459 − 0.02)(ln(1/0.98))^(1/1.483))]^(1/3) = 1601.422 lbf = 726.39 kg = 7125.91 N = 7.125 kN; catalog: 02-15 mm, C10 = 8.06, C0 = 3.65 kN [MD-REV p.19].
    • Fa/C0: Fa = 23.78 lbf = 0.1058 kN, 0.1058/3.65 written 0.28 then 0.29 (⚠ F33); interpolating the Y2 table (0.28 → 1.15, 0.42 → 1.04) gives Y2 = 1.14 [MD-REV p.19].
    • Second pass: Fe = 0.56(1)(12.75) + 1.14(23.78) = 34.2492 lbf; C10 = 1.5(34.249)[…]^(1/3) = 1192.32 lbf = 5.3 kN (a "1142.6" is also written beside it) [MD-REV p.19].
    • Next size: 02-12 mm, C10 = 7.02, C0 = 3.05 kN (chosen from 5.3 kN). Fa/C0 = 0.1058/3.05 = 0.03; interpolation (0.028 → 1.99, 0.042 → 1.85) gives Y2 = 1.97; Fe = 0.56(1)(12.75) + 1.97(23.78) = 53.9866 lbf; C10 = 1.5(53.9866)[…]^(1/3) = 1879.46 lbf = 8.363 kN [MD-REV p.20].
    • Since 8.363 kN exceeds 7.02 kN the next size is tried: 02-17 mm, C10 = 9.95, C0 = 4.75 kN; Fa/C0 = 0.105/4.75 written 0.22; interpolation (0.28 → 1.15, 0.42 → 1.04) gives Y2 = 1.197; Fe = 35.60466 lbf; C10 = 1.5(35.6047)[…]^(1/3) = 1239.52 lbf = 5.51 kN [MD-REV p.20–21].
    • The sheet then reads "C10 = 7.02, C0 = 3.05, Choose 02-12 mm" with a large X: 02-12 mm (⚠ F33) [MD-REV p.21].
  • (d) Fatigue (Soderberg wording; the working is as follows) [MD-REV p.22–24]:
    • Sut = 55 kpsi, Sy = 30 kpsi, kf = 1.6 (written 1.6 first, 1.66 later), ke = 1, kd = 1. Se = ka kb kc kd ke kf S′e with S′e = 0.5 Sut = 0.5(55) = 27.5 kpsi [MD-REV p.22].
    • ka = a Sut^b with a = 2.7, b = −0.26: ka = 2.7(55)^−0.26 = 0.95. kb = (de/0.3)^−0.107 with de = 0.808√(hb) = 0.808√(Ft); F = 1.4 in, t unknown [MD-REV p.22].
    • Lewis form: x = t²/(4L) with L = a + b = 1/Pn + 1.25/Pn = 1/12 + 1.25/12 = 0.1875 in; Y = 2xPn/3 with Y = 0.309 gives 0.309 = 2x(12)/3, x = 0.0386 in [MD-REV p.22]. Then 0.0386 = t²/(4 × 0.1875), t = 0.170 in [MD-REV p.23].
    • de = 0.808√(Ft) = 0.808√(1.4 × 0.170) = 0.394 in; kb = (0.394/0.3)^−0.107 = 0.97; kc = kd = ke = 1; kf = 1.66; Se = 0.79(0.95)(1)(1)(1)(1.66)(27.5) = 34.26 kpsi (⚠ F34) [MD-REV p.23].
    • Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1); q = 0.6; fillet radius rf = 0.3/Pn = 0.3/12 = 0.025 in; rf/d = 0.025/t = 0.025/0.170 = 0.15; D/d = 3; Kt = 1.68; Kf = 1 + 0.6(1.68 − 1) = 1.41 [MD-REV p.23].
    • Stress: σ = Kv Wt P/(F Y); Kv = (1200 + V)/1200 = (1200 + 801.1)/1200 = 1.6675; σ = 1.6675(41.193)(12)/(1.4 × 0.309) = 1905.39 psi. (An earlier "σall = 1142.67 psi = 1.14267 kpsi" is struck through.) [MD-REV p.24]
    • Criterion as written: Kf σall = Sy/n, so 1.41(1905.39/1000) = 30/n and n = 11 (boxed and circled) [MD-REV p.24] (⚠ F34).
  • Unreadable or unclear: the year of this exam is not printed; the Y2-table values are those written next to the interpolation on pp.19–20 (the table itself is not in the file); the last digit of kf in the statement is blurred [MD-REV p.12, p.19–20].

12.7 Not covered by the sources (for this section)

  • The exam papers give no marking scheme and no model answers other than the student solutions above.
  • The catalogue tables are not in the exam scans. The C10 and C0 values the solutions quote (angular-contact 02-12, 02-15, 02-17 mm; roller 02-25 and 03-25 mm) and the Y2 values 1.99, 1.85, 1.15, 1.04 agree with Tables 11-1 to 11-3 of [MD-7] (sections 9.5 and 9.6).
  • Parts (f) and (g) of PQ3 are not solved on the captured pages, and the bending safety factor of the textbook solution (PQ4) is not printed [MD-R1 p.11; MD-R2 p.4].

Calculator candidates

  1. Flat-belt tensions and slip check [MD-2 p.12–24]

    • Inputs: D, d, C (m); n (rpm); H_nom (kW); Ks; nd; b, t (m); γ (N/m³); Fa (N/m); Cp; Cv; f.
    • Chain:
      • φ = π − 2 sin⁻¹[(D − d)/2C]; V = πdn/60.
      • w = γbt; Fc = (w/g)V².
      • T = H_nom Ks nd/(2πn/60).
      • (F1)a = b Fa Cp Cv; F2 = (F1)a − 2T/d; Fi = [(F1)a + F2]/2 − Fc.
      • f′ = (1/φ) ln{[(F1)a − Fc]/(F2 − Fc)}.
    • Outputs: φ, V, Fc, T, (F1)a, F2, Fi, f′ (slip if f′ > f), nfs.

  2. V-belt drive [MD-3 p.8–21]

    • Inputs: section; d, D (mm); inside circumference Li (mm); n (rpm); H_nom (kW); Ks; nd.
    • Chain:
      • Lp = Li + Table 17-11 addition; C from (17-16b); φ from (17-1); V = πdn/60.
      • Htab from Table 17-12 (interpolate); K1 from Table 17-13 on (D − d)/C; K2 from Table 17-14.
      • Ha = K1 K2 Htab; Hd = H_nom Ks nd; Nb = ceil(Hd/Ha).
      • Fc = Kc(V/2.4)²; ΔF = (Hd/Nb)/(πn d/60) in SI, as in Ex 17-4.
      • F1 = Fc + ΔF e^(0.5123φ)/(e^(0.5123φ) − 1); F2 = F1 − ΔF; Fi = (F1 + F2)/2 − Fc.
      • nfs = Ha Nb/(H_nom Ks).
      • Life: T1 = F1 + Kb/d, T2 = F1 + Kb/D; Np = [(K/T1)^−b + (K/T2)^−b]^−1 (valid only for 10⁸–10⁹ passes).
    • Outputs: Lp, C, Nb, F1, F2, Fi, nfs, Np.

  3. Gear force components [MD-S4 p.2–6; MD-IP p.3, p.9; MD-REV p.13–14]

    • Inputs: type; H (kW); n (rpm); d (mm); φ or φn; ψ (helical); γ (bevel pinion pitch angle); λ, f (worm).
    • Chain:
      • Wt = 60 000H/(πdn) kN (or 33 000H/V lbf).
      • Spur: Wr = Wt tan φ.
      • Helical: W = Wt/(cos φn cos ψ); Wr = W sin φn; Wa = W cos φn sin ψ (φn = tan⁻¹(tan φt cos ψ)).
      • Bevel: Wr = Wt tan φ cos γ; Wa = Wt tan φ sin γ (with d = mean diameter).
      • Worm: W = W_Wt/(cos φn sin λ + f cos λ); Wʸ = W sin φn; Wᶻ = W(cos φn cos λ − f sin λ); η = (cos φn − f tan λ)/(cos φn + f cot λ).
      • T = Wt d/2.
    • Outputs: Wt, Wr, Wa, T, η.

  4. AGMA spur/helical factors of safety [MD-S5 p.1–11; SI form: MD-IP p.10–14, MD-REV p.6–11, MD-R2 p.2–4]

    • Inputs: H (hp); n (rpm); NP, NG; Pd; F (in); Qv; HB; cycles; Ko; J; Y; KR; Cp; I.
    • Chain:
      • dP = NP/Pd; V = πdn/12; Wt = 33 000H/V.
      • Kv = [(A + √V)/A]^B, with B = 0.25(12 − Qv)^(2/3) and A = 50 + 56(1 − B).
      • Ks = 1.192(F√Y/Pd)^0.0535.
      • Km = 1 + Cmc(Cpf Cpm + Cma Ce).
      • σ = Wt Ko Kv Ks (Pd/F)(Km KB/J).
      • St = 77.3HB + 12 800; YN = 1.3558N^−0.0178; SF = St YN/(KT KR σ).
      • σc = Cp[Wt Ko Kv Ks Km Cf/(dP F I)]^½.
      • Sc = 322HB + 29 100; ZN = 1.4488N^−0.023; SH = Sc ZN CH/(KT KR σc).
    • Outputs: σ, SF, σc, SH, and the threat (compare SF with SH²).

  5. Drum-brake shoe (internal or external) [MD-6 p.18–28, p.40–41]

    • Inputs: f; pa (Pa); b, r, a, c (m); θ1, θ2, θa; rotation sense; internal or external.
    • Chain:
      • Mf = (f pa b r/sin θa)[r(cos θ1 − cos θ2) − (a/2)(sin²θ2 − sin²θ1)].
      • MN = (pa b r a/sin θa)[(θ/2 − ¼ sin 2θ)] from θ1 to θ2.
      • F = (MN ∓ Mf)/c; self-locking if MN ≤ Mf.
      • T = f pa b r²(cos θ1 − cos θ2)/sin θa.
      • Reactions from (16-9)/(16-10) or (16-12)/(16-14).
    • Outputs: Mf, MN, F, T, Rx, Ry.

  6. Disk clutch / annular-pad / cone [MD-6 p.52–53, p.59–60, p.72–73; cone example MD-R1 p.2–3]

    • Inputs: D, d (or ro, ri); f; pa or F; θ2 − θ1 (pads); α (cone); number of friction faces.
    • Chain:
      • Uniform wear: F = (π pa d/2)(D − d); T = (Ff/4)(D + d).
      • Uniform pressure: F = (π pa/4)(D² − d²); T = (Ff/3)(D³ − d³)/(D² − d²).
      • Cone: divide T by sin α.
      • Pads: (16-33)–(16-40).
    • Outputs: F, T, re, r̄.

  7. Bearing C10 with reliability, and life [MD-7 p.13–28, p.37–39; MD-IP p.7, MD-R1 p.9–10, MD-REV p.4–5, p.17–21]

    • Inputs: Fr, Fa; V; ball or roller (a = 3 or 10/3); 𝓛D (h); nD (rpm); RD; af; x0, θ, b; LR; C0 (for Y2 lookup).
    • Chain:
      • Fe = X V Fr + Y Fa (Table 11-1 on Fa/C0 and e).
      • xD = 60𝓛D nD/LR.
      • C10 = af Fe{xD/[x0 + (θ − x0)(ln(1/RD))^(1/b)]}^(1/a), or the (1 − RD) approximation for R ≥ 0.90.
      • Reverse: 𝓛10 = LR/(60n)^a.
    • Outputs: Fe, xD, required C10, L10 life.

  8. Marin-corrected endurance limit and fatigue safety factor [MD-F p.1–6; tooth example MD-REV p.22–24]

    • Inputs: Sut, Sy (MPa); surface finish; d (mm); load type; T (°C); reliability %; Kt; notch radius r (for q); σa, σm.
    • Chain:
      • S′e = 0.5Sut (≤ 1400 MPa) or 700 MPa.
      • ka = aSut^b; kb from d; kc; kd (table); ke (table); Se = ka kb kc kd ke S′e.
      • Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1).
      • n from mod-Goodman σa/Se + σm/Sut = 1/n (or Soderberg, Gerber, ASME-elliptic).
    • Outputs: Se, Kf, n.

  9. Shaft bearing reactions, two planes [MD-IP p.4–6, MD-R1 p.7–8, MD-REV p.3–4, p.14–16]

    • Inputs: axial positions of the bearings and of each load along the shaft; the y and z components of each load (gear: Wt, Wr; sprocket: P; helical: Wa with its radius); shaft direction.
    • Chain:
      • ΣM about the first bearing in each plane gives the second bearing's component (y: Cy or Dy; z: Cz or Dz).
      • ΣF gives the first bearing's component; helical Wa adds a moment Wa·dp/2 and an axial reaction at the thrust bearing.
      • Total radial load per bearing = √(y² + z²) of the same bearing (⚠ F27: do not mix components of different bearings).
    • Outputs: Ay, Az, By (Dy), Bz (Dz), radial and axial load per bearing.

  10. Minimum pinion teeth without interference and module [MD-IP p.8, MD-R1 p.10, MD-REV p.5]

  • Inputs: mG (gear ratio); φ; K = 1 for full depth; pitch diameter d.
  • Chain: NP = [2K/((1 + 2mG) sin²φ)][mG + √(mG² + (1 + 2mG) sin²φ)], rounded up; NG = mG NP; m = d/N or Pd = N/d.
  • Outputs: NP (minimum, integer), NG, m or Pd.
  1. Ensemble reliability and bearing pre-selection loop [MD-IP p.6–7, MD-REV p.15–21, MD-R1 p.9–10]
  • Inputs: ensemble reliability R and number of bearings n (R_each = R^(1/n)); life ℓD (h); speed nD (rpm); af; Weibull set (Table 11-6: manufacturer 1 or 2); Fr, Fa; catalog rows (C10, C0).
  • Chain:
    • R_each = R^(1/n) (⚠ F22: 0.8145^(1/4) = 0.95).
    • xD = 60 nD ℓD/LR; C10 = af Fe{xD/[x0 + (θ − x0)(ln(1/R_each))^(1/b)]}^(1/a).
    • Iterate for angular-contact balls: Y2 from Fa/C0 (Table 11-1), Fe = 0.56 V Fr + Y2 Fa, C10 required, next catalogue row until C10(catalog) ≥ C10 required.
  • Outputs: R_each, required C10 at each pass, chosen bearing.
  1. Gear-tooth bending check by the Lewis form and fatigue [MD-REV p.22–24]
  • Inputs: Pn, F, Wt, V, Sut, Sy; Kt (chart), q, Marin factors.
  • Chain:
    • L = 1/Pn + 1.25/Pn; Y (given, or table) = 2xPn/3, so x = 3Y/(2Pn); t = √(4Lx); de = 0.808√(Ft); kb = (de/0.3)^−0.107.
    • Kv = (1200 + V)/1200; σ = Kv Wt Pn/(F Y); rf = 0.3/Pn; Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1); n = Sy/(Kf σ) as written in the source (⚠ F34: the Soderberg form with Se is the asked criterion).
  • Outputs: t, de, kb, Kf, σ, n.

⚠ Flags

  • F1 [MD-2 p.19]: the highlighted box prints "Ha = Hnom Ks nd".

    • Believed correct: Hd = Hnom Ks nd. The line above it in the text defines this as the design power Hd, and Ha is the allowable power used in nfs = Ha/(Hnom Ks) [MD-2 p.24].
    • Check: Example 17-1 calls 11(1.25)(1.1) = 15.125 kW the "design power" [MD-2 p.30–31].

  • F2 [MD-2 p.29–30]: T is computed as 82.5 N·m, but the next line uses 2(82)/0.15 = 1093.3 N.

    • With T = 82.53 N·m, ΔF = 1100.4 N, F2 = 789.6 N and Fi ≈ 1236 N instead of 796.7 N and 1240.4 N.
    • Check: 2 × 82.533/0.15 = 1100.4. This is only a rounding slip; the conclusions (no slip, nfs = 1.1) are unchanged.

  • F3 [MD-3 p.10]: Table 17-12 (SI), section A, 85 mm, 20 m/s is printed as 1.64.

    • Believed a misprint: every other row in the table peaks at 20 or 25 m/s, and at 20 m/s this value must lie between the 75 mm row (0.69) and the 95 mm row (1.49). The correct digit cannot be recovered from the source.
    • Check: 1.64 > 1.49, although power rating increases with pitch diameter in every other column.

  • F4 [MD-3 p.10]: the table title says "Horsepower Ratings", but the SI speed columns are in m/s and no power unit is printed. Example 17-4 uses the values as kW [MD-3 p.26–27].

    • Check: read the SI table as kW per belt.

  • F5 [MD-3 p.26]: Htab is interpolated at V = 17 m/s (3.506 kW), but V = π(0.188)(1750/60) = 17.23 m/s.

    • Check: at 17.23 m/s the interpolation gives 3.52 kW. Negligible, flagged only for exactness.

  • F6 [MD-2 p.24]: step 3 prints T = 63 025 Hnom Ks nd/n (US: lbf·in, hp, rpm) next to the boxed T = Hnom Ks nd/(2πn).

    • The boxed SI form needs n in rev/s (the example uses 2π·1750/60).
    • Check: Example 17-1 divides by 2π(1750/60) [MD-2 p.29]. This is a units note, not a wrong formula.

  • F7 [MD-6 p.79]: Ex 16-5 gives the rotary inertia as "289 lbm·in·s".

    • Believed correct unit: lbf·in·s². In E = ½(I/9336)(ωo² − ωf²) Btu, 9336 converts in·lbf to Btu, so I·ω² must come out in in·lbf.
    • Check: (lbf·in·s²)(s⁻²) = lbf·in. The numbers (E = 10.6 Btu) are unaffected.

  • F8 [MD-6 p.49]: the single-plate clutch sketch labels the friction surface "μs = 1.6".

    • This is implausible for a friction coefficient: Table 16-3 on the same deck lists f = 0.06–0.63 [MD-6 p.82]. The label is inside a pasted picture and is not used in any calculation. The intended value cannot be read from the source.

  • F9 [MD-S4 p.22–23], P13-57 worm (moment equation): the i-component of R_G × W is written as −287 350 − 149 466.

    • Correct: (−50)(5747) − (−100)(1494.66) = −287 350 + 149 466 = −137 884 N·mm.
    • Consequences, with the other printed values kept:
      • F_B^y = 689.4 N (not 2184.08 N), so F_B = √(318.5² + 689.4²) = 759.4 N (not 2207.18 N).
      • F_A^y = −(1494.66 + 689.4) = −2184.1 N, so the radial load at A = √(318.5² + 2184.1²) = 2207.2 N (not 3692.5 N).
      • The thrust at A (5747 N) and T = 31.85 N·m are unchanged.
    • Check: numpy cross product of (0, −50, −100) and (−637, 1494.66, 5747) gives (−137 884, 63 700, −31 850).

  • F10 [MD-S5 p.12–13], P14-20(b): Pd/F = 0.8 is solved while keeping Wt = 787.8 lbf, Kv, Ks and Km at their Pd = 6, F = 2 in values. But Wt = 33 000H/V and V ∝ dP = 16/Pd, so Wt changes with Pd.

    • With Pd = 3.2: dP = 5 in, V = 392.7 ft/min, Wt = 420.2 lbf. The real SH,P is then above 2, so the result is conservative but not the exact solution.
    • Check: 33 000 × 5/(π × 5 × 300/12) = 420.2 lbf. This is a method simplification rather than an arithmetic error; confirm with Eng. Ehsan.

  • F11 [MD-4 p.34–35, p.41]: example labels are inconsistent. The 17T/34T helical example starts as "Example 13-3" (p.34), but its continuation (p.35) is titled "Example 13-2". The 30:1 gear-train example (p.41) is also titled "Example 13-3".

    • Check: p.35 continues the Pn = 5, ψ = 30° data of p.34, not the Pt = 6, ψ = 25° data of Ex 13-2 (p.33).

  • F12 [MD-S5 p.14]: helical Cpf is written as 2/(10 × 3.097) − 0.0375 + 0.0125 × 2 = 0.0525; the pinion diameter is 3.079 in.

    • Check: with 3.079 the result is 0.05245 ≈ 0.0525, as printed. It is a transcription typo only.

  • F13 [MD-1 p.11]: in Table 1-2 the rows starting 3-85 and 3-87 both end with "13-48".

    • Every other column in those two rows advances by one (5-56/5-57, 6-43/6-44, 7-18/7-19, 11-47/11-48), so the second 13-48 may be a misprint for the next problem number. The source does not show which.

  • F14 [MD-41 p.53], Ex 13-8: the axial force is printed as "Wa = Wt tan φ cos Γ = 1865 tan 20° sin 71.6° = 644 N".

    • The symbolic form says cos Γ, but the number uses sin 71.6°, as Eq (13-38) requires (Wa = Wt tan φ sin γ, with Γ replacing γ). With cos Γ the value would be 214 N.
    • Check: 1865 tan 20° sin 71.565° = 644.0 N ✓ (the evaluated number is right; only the symbol is wrong).

  • F15 [MD-41 p.63–64], Ex 13-9: the scalar solution prints T = 128(62.3/2) = 3982 N·mm, but the vector solution on the next page gives the i-component 3987 (T = 4 kN·mm).

    • Check: 128 × 31.15 = 3987.2 N·mm. The 3982 is a small arithmetic slip.

  • F16 [MD-5 p.12, p.15], Ex 14-2: the surface factor is computed as ka = 2.70(55)^−0.265 = 0.934 (p.12), but the Marin product on p.15 uses 0.838: Se = 0.838(0.948)(1)(1)(1)1.66(27.5) = 36.3 kpsi.

    • With ka = 0.934 as computed: Se = 40.4 kpsi, σall = 40.4/[1.42(3)] = 9.48 kpsi, Wt = 346 lbf, H = 6.6 hp (instead of 36.3 kpsi, 8.52 kpsi, 311 lbf, 5.9 hp).
    • Check: 2.70 × 55^−0.265 = 0.9336. The source does not say where 0.838 comes from; confirm with the lecturer.

  • F17 [MD-5 p.23–24], Ex 14-3: the statement gives a tangential load of 382 lbf, but the substitution in Eq (14-14) uses 380.

    • Check: σC = −72 270 psi with 380 and −72 460 psi with 382; n = 1.35 or 1.34. The printed −72 400 psi and n = 1.34 are unaffected at the precision shown.

  • F18 [MD-5 p.86–87], Ex 14-5: the gear radius is written rG = 6.004/2 = 3.002 in (dG was 6.005 in on p.85) and (rb)G = 2.767 in, but Eq (14-25) is evaluated with 3.004 and 2.769.

    • Check: with consistent values (rG = 3.0022, rbG = 2.7677 in) Z = 0.4501 in (printed 0.4507), mN = 0.6903, I = 0.1950 — the same I = 0.195 to three figures. The results are unaffected.

  • F19 [MD-S1 p.10–11], P17-4: the width is printed as b = 5.6 in.

    • Solving 87.11b = 12.34(87.11b − 456.1) gives b = 12.34 × 456.1/(11.34 × 87.11) = 5.70 in (5.70 in also with the unrounded e^(0.8π) = 12.345 and Fc = 12.90b). The conclusion b = 6 in is unchanged.
    • Two notation slips on the same pages: the torque 10 946.44 is labelled "lbf/in" (it is lbf·in), and the friction line is written "π × 0.8 = (1/π) ln(…)"; the next line, e^(0.8π) = …, uses the correct form 0.8π = ln(…).

  • F20 [MD-4 p.9 = MD-41 p.9 against MD-S3 p.8], Table 13-4: the lecture slide prints the normal arc tooth thickness as π/Pn − Bn/2, while the section handout prints π/(2Pn) − Bn/2.

    • π/Pn is the whole normal circular pitch pn (tooth plus space), so a tooth thickness of about half of it, π/(2Pn) − Bn/2, is the consistent form. The lecture version is believed to be the misprint (it is reproduced as printed in 4.1).

  • F21 [MD-IMP p.1 against MD-1 p.3]: the student note says the course is out of 150 marks (50 coursework + 100 final), while the Design (2) syllabus slide gives CW 50 (50%) + FE 50 (50%) = 100.

    • The two may describe different years or a different scaling; the sources do not say which applies now. Confirm the current mark distribution with the department.

  • F22 [MD-IP p.6–7], PQ1(c): the ensemble reliability of four bearings is solved as R = (0.8145)^(1/4) = 0.90249 ≈ 0.9025, then the C10 line uses (1 − 0.9025).

    • Correct: 0.95⁴ = 0.8145, so R = 0.95 per bearing (0.9025 = 0.95²). The countershaft speed is also rounded, nC = 95 instead of 191/2 = 95.5 (xD = 68.4 instead of 68.76).
    • Consequences with the printed data: C10 = 11.70 kN with R = 0.95 and xD = 68.4 (11.72 kN with 95.5 rev/min), against the printed 10.111 kN (which reproduces with R = 0.9025).
    • Check: 2425.268[68.4/(0.02 + 4.439(1 − 0.9025)^(1/1.483))]^(1/3) = 10 111.7 N; with (1 − 0.95) it is 11 702.5 N.

  • F23 [MD-IP p.11], PQ1(g): Kv is computed as (A + √(200V))/A = 1.26 with the exponent B = 0.825 missing.

    • Check: with V = 1.25 m/s, A = 59.77 (59.8), B = 0.8255: (59.77 + √250)/59.77 = 1.2645; with the exponent Kv = 1.2138. The same slip is made in [MD-REV p.7] (see F28); [MD-R2 p.2] applies the exponent (1.69).
    • With Kv = 1.214 and the other printed factors: σ = 14.73 MPa, SF = 33.4; the printed 15.287 MPa and 32.14 use 1.26.

  • F24 [MD-IP p.14], PQ1(h): the contact stress is printed as σc = 191 × 1869.38 √(N/m²) → 357.05 MPa, but the printed factors give a smaller root.

    • Check: 1600(1.26)(1.172)(1.4115)/[(0.125)(0.1047156)(0.107)] = 2.381 × 10⁶, root 1543, so σc = 191 × 1.543 = 294.6 MPa (294.7 MPa with rounded values), not 357.05 MPa. The arithmetic 191 × 1.8693 = 357.0 is right; the 1869 root is not reproduced.
    • Then SH = 1551(0.9415)/(0.8854)/294.6 = 5.60, against the printed 4.619 (which reproduces with 357.05). With the exponent of Kv (F23) as well: σc = 289.1 MPa, SH = 5.71.

  • F25 [MD-R1 p.2], PQ2 uniform wear: the substitution prints (12² − 1²) = 143 where the formula needs (D² − d²) = 12² − 11² = 23.

    • The printed pa = 2.25 lbf/in² and F = 38.87 lbf follow from 143. Correct: pa = 1800 × 8 sin 12.53°/[π(0.281)(11)(23)] = 13.99 psi and F = π pa d(D − d)/2 = π(13.99)(11)(1)/2 = 241.7 lbf.
    • This agrees with the uniform-pressure result (13.4 psi, 242 lbf) [MD-R1 p.2–3]. Also α is 12.53° in one place and 12.58° in another (sin α = 0.5/2.305 gives 12.53°; the effect on pa is 0.1 %).

  • F26 [MD-R1 p.9–10], PQ3(c): the reliability term is evaluated as (1 − R) = (1 − 0.95), while [MD-REV] uses ln(1/R); [MD-IP p.7] also uses (1 − R).

    • Shigley's Weibull form (Eq 11-9 in [MD-7]) uses ln(1/RD); (1 − R) is its first-order approximation. With ln(1/R): C10 = 4549 lbf (O) and 12 040.7 lbf (C), against the printed 4574.41 and 12 107.72 lbf.
    • Check: 1.3(332.746)[720/(0.02 + 4.439(ln(1/0.95))^(1/1.483))]^(1/3) = 4549.1 lbf. The difference is 0.6 %. Not an error, but the two methods are used inconsistently in the sources.

  • F27 [MD-REV p.4–5], PQ4(b), (c): the bearing totals mix components. FO,tot = √(5.08² + 8.3189²) = 9.747 kN combines Oy with Cy, and FC,tot = √(0.49² + 10.83²) = 10.841 kN combines Oz with Cz.

    • Correct: FO = √(Oy² + Oz²) = √(5.08² + 0.49²) = 5.107 kN and FC = √(Cy² + Cz²) = √(8.3189² + 10.83²) = 13.655 kN.
    • Consequences (with the printed method, ln(1/R)): C10(O) = 76.0 kN (printed 145.07 kN); C10(C) = 203.2 kN (printed 161.36 kN). The components (Oy = 5.08, Cy = 8.3189, Oz = 0.49, Cz = 10.83) reproduce ✓.
    • Check: 1.2(5.107)[648/(0.02 + 4.439(ln(1/0.98))^(1/1.483))]^(1/3) = 76.0 kN.

  • F28 [MD-REV p.7], PQ4(f): Kv = (59.7776 + √(200 × 14.137))/59.7776 = 1.89 omits the exponent B = 0.8254; [MD-R2 p.2] applies it and gets 1.69.

    • Check: (59.7776 + 53.17)/59.7776 = 1.8896; 1.8896^0.8254 = 1.691.
    • With Kv = 1.69 and the other MD-REV factors (Ks = 1.28, KH = 1.4377, J = 0.275): σ = 52.95 MPa (MD-R2 gets 53.9 MPa with KH = 1.44, J = 0.27); σc ≈ 456 MPa with I = 0.1596. Printed: σ = 59.18 MPa, σc = 482.6 MPa, SH = 1.86.

  • F29 [MD-REV p.9], PQ4(f): YN = 1.3558(648 × 10⁶)^−0.0178 is printed as 1.95; the value is 0.945 (with the printed −0.0178, [MD-R2 p.3] reads YN = 0.9 from Fig 14-14). KR uses 0.079 (0.967) where [MD-R2 p.3] uses 0.0759 (0.955).

    • The printed SF = 323.9(1.95)/(1 × 0.967)/59.18 evaluates to 11.03, which is the value written first and struck out; the boxed 5.65 corresponds to YN ≈ 0.90 (0.945 gives 5.35; the [MD-R2] numbers give 324(0.9)/0.955/53.9 = 5.665). The source does not say how 5.65 was obtained.
    • Check: 1.3558 × (6.48 × 10⁸)^−0.0178 = 0.9448; 0.658 − 0.0759 ln(0.02) = 0.9549; 0.658 − 0.079 ln(0.02) = 0.9670.

  • F30 [MD-R2 p.2 against MD-REV p.10], PQ4: the geometry factor I. [MD-REV p.10] uses φt = 25° for gear B (I = cos 25° sin 25°/2 × 5/6 = 0.1596, printed 0.1595 / 0.1593); [MD-R2 p.2] uses 20° (I = cos 20° sin 20°/2 × 5/6 = 0.134) although Wt = FB cos 25°.

    • The pressure angle of gear B is 25° in the exam statement and figure [MD-REV p.2]. With I = 0.1596 and the [MD-R2] factors: σc = 456 MPa and SH = 1.87, against the printed 498 MPa and 1.72.
    • [MD-R2 p.2] also prints B = 0.25(12 − Q)^(2/3) as "(12 − 6)^(2/3) = 0.8255" without the 0.25, and A = 50 + 56(1 − B) as "50 + (1 − 0.8255)" without the 56; the results 0.8255 and 59.77 are the correct values.

  • F31 [MD-R2 p.1–2 against MD-R1 p.4], PQ4: the textbook statement (Shigley 14-38) says "20° spur gears" and the US figure has FB at 20°, but the solution works in SI with φ = 25° for gear B (as in the exam figure [MD-REV p.2]) and with d = 300 mm; the US figure shows gear B of 8 in (203 mm).

    • Also ΣMx = 0 is printed as "300(11) cos 20 − 150 FB cos 25", mixing mm and kN; the numbers are right (radii 300 and 150 mm, FA = 11 kN: FB = 22.81 kN).
    • Check: 11 cos 20°(300)/(150 cos 25°) = 22.81 kN ✓. [MD-R2 p.1–2] is the SI version of the figure on [MD-REV p.2].

  • F32 [MD-REV p.13–16], PQ5(a): the tangential load is printed as Wt = 40.493 lbf, but every later step uses 41.193 lbf.

    • Wr = 17.31 and Wa = 23.78 lbf correspond to 41.193 (17.30 and 23.78); with 40.493 they would be 17.01 and 23.38 lbf. T = 41.193(0.865) = 35.632 lbf·in gives nD = 63 025/35.632 = 1768.77 rev/min instead of the given 1800; this 1768.77 is then used for xD of the ball bearing at A (4245.6) but 1800 for the roller B (xD = 48).
    • Also V is written 815.24 ft/min in one line, 815.1 in the Wt line, and 801.1 in the Kv of part (d) (Kv = (1200 + 801.1)/1200 = 1.6675; with 815.24, Kv = 1.679).
    • Check: 33 000(1)/[π(1.7321)(1800)/12] = 40.43 lbf; 41.193 does not follow from the data (the 40.493 printed is 33 000/815.1).

  • F33 [MD-REV p.17–21], PQ5(b), (c): bearing selection.

    • Fa/C0 is printed 0.29 for Fa = 0.1058 kN and C0 = 3.65 kN; the ratio is 0.029. Likewise 0.1058/4.75 = 0.0223 is printed 0.22. Only the 02-12 mm case (0.0347 ≈ 0.03) is right. The Y2 values 1.14 and 1.197 come from the wrong ratios; the table interpolation for 0.03 gives 1.97 [MD-REV p.19–20].
    • By the source's own steps, 02-12 mm (C10 = 7.02 kN) needs C10 = 8.363 kN with the correct Y2 = 1.97, so it is too small, and 02-17 mm (9.95 kN) would be the first adequate size; the final "Choose 02-12 mm" rests on the wrong Y2 = 1.197.
    • For the roller bearing B the requirement is C10 = 1.7 kN [MD-REV p.17] but the written choice is 02-25 mm (16.8 kN) or 03-25 mm (28.6 kN); the source does not say why such a large bearing is chosen (no shaft diameter is given), and it is unclear which of the two is the answer.
    • Check: 0.1058/3.65 = 0.0290; 0.1058/3.05 = 0.0347; 0.1058/4.75 = 0.0223; 1.5(53.9866)[4245.6/…]^(1/3) = 1879.5 lbf = 8.36 kN.

  • F34 [MD-REV p.23–24], PQ5(d): fatigue.

    • Se is printed as 0.79(0.95)(1)(1)(1)(1.66)(27.5) = 34.26 kpsi, but kb was just computed as 0.97 (0.79 is not derived). With 0.97: Se = 42.07 kpsi.
    • The final relation used is Kf σ = Sy/n (1.41 × 1.905 = 30/n, n = 11), i.e. Sy only; the problem asks for a Soderberg (Se, Sy) infinite-life estimate and Se is not used. The margin formula KF σall = S…/nd suggests Se. With Se = 34.26 kpsi and a fully reversed bending stress, n = 34.26/(1.41 × 1.905) = 12.75 (15.66 with Se = 42.07); this is a recomputation, not in the source.
    • kf: "kf = 1.6" (first line, and the statement) and "kf = 1.66" (later lines) are both written; Kf (stress concentration) = 1.41 and kf (Marin factor, 1.66) are different symbols.

  • F35 [MD-REV p.17], PQ5(b): the cylindrical roller bearing at B is rated with the manufacturer 1 parameters (LR = 90 × 10⁶, x0 = 0, θ = 4.48, b = 1.5, a = 10/3).

    • Table 11-6 of [MD-7] lists manufacturer 1 for tapered roller bearings and manufacturer 2 (LR = 10⁶, x0 = 0.02, θ = 4.459, b = 1.483) for ball and straight roller bearings [MD-7 section 9.4]. The statement does not name a manufacturer for this part.
    • With manufacturer 2 (a = 10/3, xD = 60(1800)(40 000)/10⁶ = 4320): C10 = 1.5(57.32)[4320/(0.02 + 4.439(ln(1/0.98))^(1/1.483))]^(0.3) = 1465 lbf = 6.52 kN, against the printed 382.2 lbf = 1.7 kN. Either way the written choice of 25 mm (16.8 kN) is larger than needed (F33).
